brief: Goldman Sachs (Robert Quinn) reports Nasdaq Non-Dealer net futures positioning dipped negative and then rebounded through August on CFTC Commitment of Traders data. Non-Dealers bought every week from August 4 to September 1 for a cumulative +$51.3bn, a record stretch in notional terms. The driver is mostly hedge unwind rather than fresh risk: Hedge Funds were +$37.5bn, almost entirely covering (+$38.6bn), consistent with Nasdaq 3 month implied volatility cheapening outright and relative to S&P, normalized 25 delta put-call skew rising, and hedges closing as cash longs were sold. Genuine demand also surfaced. Asset Manager bought +$4.4bn (gross longs +$5bn over shorts -$600mm) and Non-Reportable added +$12bn (long initiations +$4.9bn, downside reduction +$7.1bn), with Other the sole seller at -$2.6bn. That support left Nasdaq (-2.2%) down less than Russell 2k (-3.9%) and funding richened, despite rotation from Semiconductors (-5.6%) to Software (+2.3%), widening Hyperscaler credit spreads, an oil spike and higher probability of a September Fed hike. Therefore, with the 2 year rank at 92% on September 1 and 84% for Asset Manager alone, positioning is relatively high entering a busy micro and macro calendar.
